svg.title: Track the chain through translation
svg.desc: Before transfer, the growing chain is on the P-site tRNA and the incoming amino acid on A-site tRNA. After transfer, the longer chain is on A-site tRNA. Translocation moves the peptidyl-tRNA to P, while the ribosome advances toward the mRNA three-prime end. Release factors at an A-site stop promote hydrolysis of the P-site ester.
svg.text: Translation: follow the chain, then the ribosome
1 Peptide transfer
P: chain–tRNA
A: amino acid–tRNA
→ longer chain on A-site tRNA; P-site tRNA is uncharged.
No extra ATP/GTP hydrolysis for peptide-transfer chemistry.
2 Translocation
P: uncharged tRNA
A: longer chain–tRNA
→ uncharged tRNA goes to E; peptidyl-tRNA moves A → P.
EF-G + GTP in bacteria; ribosome advances 5′ → 3′ on mRNA.
3 Termination
P: completed chain–tRNA
A: stop + release factor
→ hydrolyze P-site ester; free the completed polypeptide.
Ordinary termination uses a release factor rather than a tRNA.
Keep energy costs separate
Charging: 1 ATP → AMP = 2 high-energy bond equivalents.
Ideal elongation: 1 GTP for selection + 1 GTP for translocation.
Initiation, termination, recycling and rejected substrates add costs.
